deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a clean handwritten copy of an administrative passage from the Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des sciences (Paris), page 1423, headed 'Conditions communes à tous les Concours'. It makes two points. First, the Academy will not return any work submitted to its prize competitions, though authors may have copies made at the Secrétariat de l'Institut. Second, by a general rule adopted in 1865, every prize competition closes at the same time of year, namely 1 June. The next page cites 'Comptes Rendus. 14 Juin 1869. pag. 1409' (the programme of prizes for 1871, including the Grand prix de Mathématiques). So this page belongs to the same 1869 programme, which appeared about three years after Riemann's death in July 1866. Riemann therefore cannot have written it. It is very probably in another hand, perhaps an editor or archivist (Dedekind, H. Weber, or a later Göttingen curator). It would have been filed with the 'Wärmeleitung' papers because of the Paris Academy prize question on heat conduction: Riemann submitted his 1861 'Commentatio mathematica' to that competition, and the Academy withdrew the question in 1868 without awarding the prize. There is no derivation to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors. Attributing this page to Riemann himself is chronologically impossible: the source text dates from 1869 and he died in 1866. It is a later archival or editorial insertion in the bundle.

results.what: Copy of the general rules of the Paris Academy prize competitions: submitted works are not returned, and all competitions close on 1 June (rule of 1865).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a non-mathematical copy of a Comptes Rendus prize announcement dated after Riemann's death. It is of minor archival interest only, as documentation of the Paris heat-conduction prize context for his 1861 Commentatio.

checkable.asserts: The copied Comptes Rendus text (1869) postdates Riemann's death (1866), so the page is not in Riemann's hand / not his composition.

transcription_corrections: Where the transcription has 'Sécrétariat', the manuscript appears to read 'Sécrétariat' with the copyist's accent (standard spelling 'Secrétariat').
'prévenus' is written with a looped v that resembles 'préoenus'; 'prévenus' is the correct reading.
'premier juin' is underlined in the original.
